primary.poolable_reason: 2 TRIALS, AND NO TWO SHARE A REGISTERED PRIMARY OUTCOME FAMILY. Registrations read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18: NCT00589693, NCT00986102. Their registered primaries are recorded per trial on this object and do not reduce to a common quantity, so there is nothing for two of them to estimate in common. primary.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that any trial here is poor -- each is registered and reports its own primary. NOT that the drug or intervention is ineffective. NOT that no poolable question exists in this area: only that the question this page's title asks cannot be answered by pooling the trials this page carries. THE CRITICISM IS OF THE POOLING AND OF NOTHING ELSE -- a trial that registers the endpoints it was designed to measure is behaving correctly. The registry is a live document and this reads its contents on the date recorded; a later amendment could change it. If a further eligible trial is identified, this verdict should be revisited.
